errors.wrong: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, you must do to the exact same side or the opposite side to keep it balanced.
errors.correct: Do the same thing to BOTH sides of an equation to keep it balanced.

edits.before: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, you must do to the exact same side or the opposite side to keep it balanced. To isolate a variable, you undo whatever operation is currently applied to it by using its opposite, or inverse, operation. Addition and subtraction are inverses of each other, and multiplication and division are inverses of each other.
edits.after: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, you must also do to the other side to keep it balanced. To isolate a variable, you undo whatever operation is currently applied to it by using its opposite, or inverse, operation. Addition and subtraction are inverses of each other, and multiplication and division are inverses of each other.
